conceptZh: 枝是從樹幹長出去的細枝條
object: a barrel-shaped toy pirate, his reluctant parrot, and a comically tiny twig and huge tree trunk
morph: the pirate struggles with a branch far too small and a trunk far too large, joining the wood radical 木 on the left with the 支 on the right to make 枝
creativeAngle: 海盜拿到一根比他的手指還小的樹枝，旁邊卻有一根超大木頭，大小錯亂逼他想辦法；詞用「樹枝」，鸚鵡把小枝當牙籤。
promptEn: An 8-second 3D animated toy clip on a clean solid pale cream-green backdrop, locked camera. The only text is the single Traditional Chinese glyph 枝, centered in saturated forest-brown strokes about 70 percent of frame height, with the wood radical 木 on the left and the 支 part with its cross bar and slanted legs on the right. Cast: Barnaby, a round barrel-shaped toy pirate with a bushy stitched beard, and Polly, a parrot who flatly refuses to do what he asks. Moment one, 0 to 1.8s: Barnaby proudly carries in a tiny twig no bigger than a matchstick, holding it with two fingers as if it were a mighty mast, and tries to fit it onto a trunk-shaped wooden block that is three times his height. The first 枝 is spoken as the trunk thuds down. Moment two, 1.8 to 3.4s: the twig will not stick; he hammers it with his hat, it bounces off, and Polly grabs the twig in her beak and uses it as a toothpick, shaking her head no when he reaches for it. The second 枝 is spoken as the trunk shifts its weight and the wood radical 木 forms on the left with a vertical and two sloping strokes. Moment three, 3.4s to 5.0s: Barnaby scratches his beard, looks at the huge trunk, then at the tiny twig, and snaps his fingers; he rolls a barrel against the trunk to climb it, drags a long thin plank up as the 支 horizontal and diagonal strokes, and the cross bar drops into place, completing 枝. Moment four, 5.0s onward: Polly finally hands the tiny twig back and Barnaby plants it in the bottom corner like a flag. From 5.0 to 8.0s the glyph is perfectly still and uncovered while Barnaby stands next to a tiny planted twig, saluting it with a happy hop, and Polly rocks gently on his shoulder, never touching the strokes. Audio: a warm friendly off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin says exactly 「枝、枝、樹枝」, slowly with clear tones as ㄓ、ㄓ、ㄕㄨˋ ㄓ. First 枝 near 0.7s, second near 2.4s, and 樹枝 around 5.3s as the little twig is planted. Stop after the word. Only soft wooden thunks, no background music. Soft studio lighting, vivid not neon colors, no flashing, no lens flare, no watermark, no subtitles, no vocabulary text, and no writing other than the single glyph 枝.

conceptZh: 消防隊長想幫光禿禿的小樹澆水，大怪獸轉身撞開水泵，失控的水管把隊長彈得地板、牆壁、天花板、怪獸頭四處亂撞，每撞一下就敲正一組木條，最後拼成「枝」，隊長像小鳥一樣停在最高的筆畫頂端，水管最後噴一下，小樹冒出一根新樹枝。
object: a heap of eight walnut-brown wooden slats lying on the floor like dropped firewood, which become the strokes of 枝; a chunky red toy fire engine with a fat runaway hose; a tiny clay pot holding one bare drooping twig
morph: the hose's recoil launches the toy firefighter clinging to the nozzle into a four-bounce ricochet (floor, wall, ceiling, monster's head); each bounce's thud clacks two slats upright, building 木 on the left then 支 on the right, and the final limp hose sneeze sprays the pot so a leafy branch springs out as 樹枝 is spoken
creativeAngle: 上一版是海盜把小樹枝插在大樹幹上的安靜對比笑點，這版改成全新的「彈跳連鎖」肢體喜劇：失控水管的反作用力把消防隊長當成彈珠在畫面裡四處亂彈，每一次撞擊都「喀」一聲敲正一組筆畫，動作本身就在蓋字。大怪獸只當一個會被壓扁的毛茸茸緩衝墊，不搶戲。字義也被演出來：隊長最後像小鳥停在「樹枝」上，而水管最後一噴讓小樹真的長出新枝，聽到「樹枝」的瞬間畫面正好出現樹枝。
promptEn:
An 8-second 3D toy-animation clip, locked camera, flat pale cream-blue backdrop, soft studio light. The only text ever on screen is the single Traditional Chinese glyph 枝, centered, in saturated solid walnut-brown strokes about 70 percent of frame height with clear margins: the wood radical 木 on the left, and 支 on the right with its cross bar, vertical, and the 又 legs below. At the start its eight strokes lie in a loose heap of wooden slats in the center of the floor like dropped firewood.

Lead: Chief Puddle, a stubby glossy toy firefighter figure with a painted yellow helmet and a determined chin, riding a chunky red toy fire engine whose fat grey hose has a mind of its own. Buddy: Mossy, a huge round teal fuzzball monster with one stubby horn and a goofy grin, about half the glyph's height, who knocks things over just by turning around.

0 to 1.5s: the engine squeals in from the left and parks bottom-left. Chief hops down, points hard at a drooping bare twig in a tiny clay pot bottom-right, grabs the hose nozzle and plants his feet. The first 枝 is spoken as he takes aim.

1.5 to 3s: he cranks the valve; one sad drop plops out. He shakes the nozzle and peers into it. Mossy waddles in behind the engine, turns around to see what is happening, and his fuzzy rump bumps the pump lever to full. The hose snaps rigid, roars a white water jet skyward, and the recoil launches Chief clinging to the nozzle like a rocket.

3 to 4.8s, the bounce chain: BOING off the floor, and the thud clacks the 木 horizontal and vertical upright; BONK off the left wall, and the two slanted 木 strokes swing in; BOING off the ceiling, and the 支 cross bar and vertical clack on; BONK off the top of Mossy's fuzzy head, which squashes like a pillow, and the two 又 legs snap into place, finishing 枝. The second 枝 is spoken mid-chain as strokes are snapping. The hose goes limp and Chief drops seated on the very top tip of the tallest stroke, like a bird perched on a branch, his tiny body entirely above the glyph so every stroke stays uncovered, helmet spinning, dizzy grin.

4.8 to 8s: the glyph stays perfectly still, centered and fully readable. At about 5.4s the limp hose gives one last sneeze of spray onto the potted twig and a fresh leafy green branch springs out of it with a boing; the word 樹枝 is spoken exactly on that pop. Mossy hugs the pot in delight, Chief swings his legs and gives a thumbs-up from his perch, and neither touches any stroke through the end.

Audio: a warm friendly off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin says exactly 「枝、枝、樹枝」, read as ㄓ、ㄓ、ㄕㄨˋ ㄓ, slowly with clear tones: first 枝 near 0.8s, second 枝 near 3.6s, 樹枝 near 5.4s, then stop. Only soft cartoon boings, wooden clacks and a water whoosh, no music louder than the voice. Bright not neon colors, no flashing, no lens flare, no watermark, no subtitles, no vocabulary text, no writing other than the single glyph 枝.
